findings.title: 204 register/list endpoints return entire result set with no pagination (unbounded findAll-style queries)
findings.cvss: High likelihood (every tenant's registers grow monotonically and are read on dashboard load), high impact (full table materialised into memory + serialised to JSON on every request). Not a confidentiality/integrity issue, so not Critical, but a realistic availability/latency risk as data volume grows — effectively a self-inflicted DoS vector.
findings.description: Across the backend (231 @RestController classes, 375 repositories) only 122 GET endpoints return a Spring Data Page<T>; another 332 GET endpoints return a raw List<T>/Set<T> with no Pageable parameter. Of those, 204 are collection-root 'register' endpoints (the mapping path has no {id} segment, e.g. GET /api/v1/compliance/obligations, GET /api/v1/outsourcing/arrangements, GET /api/audit-lc/findings, GET /api/v1/asm/assets) and 128 are sub-resource lists scoped under a parent /{id}/.... The register-root endpoints each fetch every non-deleted, org-scoped row for the tenant and serialise the whole set to JSON on every call. These are the exact endpoints the bilingual SPA loads on page navigation (the ObligationController Javadoc even states the register is 'wall-mounted on every dashboard'). As tenants accumulate obligations, findings, vendors, assets, DSR cases, etc., each call materialises an ever-larger list into the JVM heap and the HTTP response, with no upper bound. The canonical /api/v1/risk/risks endpoint (RiskController.java:30-35) shows the project already knows the correct pattern — Page<RiskResponse> with @PageableDefault(size = 20) — but it was applied inconsistently and most later modules regressed to raw List.
findings.rootCause: No architectural enforcement that list endpoints must be paginated. Sprint-1 core modules (risk, incident, compliance controls/findings/assessments, evidence items, IAM users, TPRM vendors, audit-log) adopted Page<T> + @PageableDefault, but the dozens of modules added in later sprints (data-officer, obligation register, outsourcing, ASM, BCM cycle, SOC-ops, sustainability, NDI, ethics, etc.) return List<T> directly from service methods that call repository finders such as findByOrganisationIdAndIsDeletedFalseOrderBy...(orgId) which have no Pageable overload. There is no global cap on page size either (see PERF-PG-003), so the platform has no backstop.
findings.evidence:
Static scan of src/main/java/**/controller/*.java:
  GET endpoints returning Page<>  (paginated):           122
  GET endpoints returning raw List/Set (unbounded):      332
     - collection-root 'register' style (no /{id}):      204
     - sub-resource (under /{id}/...):                   128
Verified register examples (controller -> service -> repository, all unbounded):
  ObligationController.list()  -> ObligationService.list() [line 74-77]
     -> ObligationRepository.findByOrganisationIdAndIsDeletedFalseOrderByNextDueDateAsc(orgId)  // returns List<Obligation>, no Pageable
  OutsourcingController.list() -> OutsourcingService.listArrangements() [line 183-186]
     -> OutsourcingArrangementRepository.findByOrganisationIdOrderByCreatedAtDesc(orgId) [line 17]  // List, no Pageable
  AttackSurfaceController.listAssets() -> AttackSurfaceAssetService.listAssets() [line 107-111]
     -> findByOrganisationIdAndIsDeletedFalseOrderByCreatedAtDesc(orgId)  // List, no Pageable
  data_officer/DataOfficerController: 14 register-root List endpoints (/dsr,/consents,/dpia,/breaches,/notices,/retention-rules,/catalog,/lineage,/disposals,/quality/rules,/quality/runs,/ndr,/ethics,/timeline)
     e.g. listDsr() -> dsrRepo.findByOrganisationIdOrderByCreatedAtDesc(org())  // List, no Pageable
findings.impact: Per-request memory and bandwidth scale linearly with the tenant's register size, with no ceiling. A single tenant with, say, 50k attack-surface assets or audit findings turns one dashboard load into a multi-MB JSON payload plus a full-table Hibernate fetch and entity-to-DTO mapping of the entire set. Under concurrency this drives heap pressure / long GC pauses / OOM and elevated p99 latency for ALL tenants on the shared JVM. Because the SPA fires several of these register calls on each page open, the effect compounds. It is also a low-effort denial-of-service primitive: any authenticated read-only user can repeatedly hit the largest register endpoint.
findings.reproduction:
1. Seed a tenant with a large register (e.g. INSERT many rows into compliance.obligation or asm.attack_surface_asset for organisation_id = 1).
2. Authenticate as any READ role and call GET /api/v1/compliance/obligations (or /api/v1/asm/assets, /api/v1/outsourcing/arrangements, /api/v1/data-officer/dsr).
3. Observe that the response contains every row for the org with no page metadata, no 'size'/'page' query params honoured, and response size + latency grow linearly with row count. Compare with GET /api/v1/risk/risks which returns a paged envelope (content/totalElements/...) and caps at 20 by default.
findings.resolution: Standardise every collection-root list endpoint on Spring Data pagination, mirroring RiskController: accept @PageableDefault(size = 20) Pageable and return Page<T>; add a paged repository overload (Page<T> findByOrganisationId...(orgId, Pageable)). Keep a small number of intentionally-unbounded helper endpoints (e.g. SCM /vendors/all 'for dropdowns') but (a) rename them explicitly, (b) hard-cap them server-side (e.g. PageRequest.of(0, 500)), and (c) document the cap. Also add a global maximum page size (see PERF-PG-003) so the Page<> endpoints cannot be abused via ?size=. Prioritise the highest-cardinality registers first: ASM assets/findings, data-officer (DSR/consents/breaches/catalog), obligations, outsourcing arrangements, audit findings, BCM BIA, policy documents.
references: OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023) API4:2023 Unrestricted Resource Consumption

findings.title: TPRM /assessments loads ALL vendors via Pageable.unpaged() then runs an unbounded IN-clause over every vendor id
findings.cvss: Medium: the endpoint is reachable by any TPRM:READ user and degrades super-linearly with vendor count (full vendor scan + a single IN-list with one parameter per vendor). Lower blast radius than PERF-PG-001 because vendor counts are typically smaller than asset/finding registers, but the explicit use of Pageable.unpaged() defeats the very pagination the module otherwise offers.
findings.description: GET /api/v1/tprm/assessments (no vendorId param) calls TprmService.listAssessments(null). The implementation first fetches EVERY vendor for the tenant using vendorRepo.findByOrganisationId(orgId, Pageable.unpaged()) — explicitly disabling pagination — maps them to a List<Long> of ids, then calls assessmentRepo.findByVendorIdIn(vendorIds), which has no Pageable and emits a SQL IN (?, ?, ... ) with one bind parameter per vendor. The result List<VendorAssessment> contains every assessment for the org. So a single request does a full vendor table scan plus a full assessment fetch, with the IN-list growing with vendor count. SQL Server has a practical/parser ceiling on IN-list and parameter counts (and a 2100-parameter limit), so beyond a few thousand vendors this can also fail outright rather than merely being slow.
findings.rootCause: The list endpoint returns the full register but the data model has no direct organisation_id on VendorAssessment, so the author worked around it by materialising all vendor ids client-side (in the service) and using findByVendorIdIn. Pageable.unpaged() was used to grab the whole vendor set, which is the anti-pattern.
findings.impact: Two unbounded fetches per request plus a parameterised IN-clause that scales with vendor count. On large tenants this is both slow (two full result sets into the heap) and potentially failing (SQL Server parameter/IN-list ceiling), turning a routine register read into an error or a long-running query that holds a DB connection.
findings.reproduction:
1. Seed many vendors and assessments for organisation_id = 1.
2. Call GET /api/v1/tprm/assessments (omit vendorId).
3. Enable Hibernate SQL logging and observe (a) SELECT of all vendors, (b) a single SELECT ... WHERE vendor_id IN (?, ?, ...) with one bind var per vendor, and the full assessment list returned with no page envelope. Scale vendors past a few thousand to hit the IN/parameter ceiling.
findings.resolution: Add organisation_id (or a join) to VendorAssessment and a paged org-scoped finder: Page<VendorAssessment> findByOrganisationId(Long orgId, Pageable pageable). Change the controller to return Page<VendorAssessment> with @PageableDefault and the service to delegate directly to the paged finder, eliminating both the Pageable.unpaged() vendor scan and the IN-list. For the vendorId-scoped branch, accept a Pageable and return a Page instead of .getContent().
references: SQL Server limit of 2100 parameters per statement

findings.title: No global maximum page size — paginated Page<> endpoints accept arbitrary ?size= and can be coerced to return all rows
findings.category: Unbounded result set / missing page-size cap
findings.cvss: Medium: turns the otherwise-correct Page<> endpoints (risk, incident, compliance, evidence, users, vendors, cyber, etc.) back into unbounded queries on demand. Any authenticated reader can request ?size=2147483647 and force a full-table fetch, so the pagination defence is bypassable.
findings.description: The project relies on @PageableDefault(size = 20) for the DEFAULT page size, but there is no configured maximum. A scan for spring.data.web.pageable.max-page-size / PageableHandlerMethodArgumentResolver.setMaxPageSize / maxPageSize across src/main returned no matches, so Spring's resolver uses its built-in default behaviour where the client-supplied ?size= overrides the default with no server-side ceiling. Consequently every 'correctly paginated' endpoint — e.g. GET /api/v1/risk/risks?size=1000000, GET /api/v1/admin/users?size=1000000, GET /api/v1/incidents?size=1000000 — will attempt to fetch and serialise that many rows in one page, re-introducing exactly the unbounded-result-set problem the Page<> envelope was meant to prevent. AuditLogController even hand-rolls page/size as plain @RequestParam(defaultValue = "100") int size with no clamp, so the same applies there.
findings.rootCause: Spring Data web pagination ships without a max page size unless one is configured; the platform never set spring.data.web.pageable.max-page-size (nor clamped hand-rolled size params), so the per-endpoint @PageableDefault only constrains the default, not the maximum a caller may request.
findings.evidence:
grep -rniE 'max-page-size|maxPageSize|setMaxPageSize|PageableHandlerMethodArgumentResolver|spring.data.web' src/main  ->  (no matches)
RiskController.java:32  @PageableDefault(size = 20, sort = "createdAt") Pageable pageable   // default only; no max
AuditLogController.java:38-39  @RequestParam(defaultValue="0") int page, @RequestParam(defaultValue="100") int size  // unclamped
Result: ?size=<arbitrary> is honoured on all Page<> endpoints, defeating pagination.
findings.impact: The pagination control protecting ~122 endpoints is bypassable by a query parameter. A single authenticated user can issue ?size=2_000_000_000 against the largest register and force a full-table fetch + serialisation, reproducing the heap pressure / latency / OOM risk of PERF-PG-001 even on the modules that were done correctly. It also undermines any fix for PERF-PG-001 unless the cap is added at the same time.
findings.reproduction: 1. Authenticate as any READ user. 2. Call GET /api/v1/risk/risks?size=1000000 (or /api/v1/admin/users?size=1000000, /api/v1/audit-log?size=1000000). 3. Observe the server attempts to return up to that many rows in one page (no clamp); response size and DB fetch scale with the requested size rather than being capped.
findings.resolution: Set a global maximum page size via configuration (spring.data.web.pageable.max-page-size: 100) so the resolver clamps any oversized ?size=. For hand-rolled size params (AuditLogController, CyberController pageOf, etc.), clamp explicitly with Math.min(size, MAX). Optionally also set spring.data.web.pageable.default-page-size to centralise the default. Combine with PERF-PG-001 so that both the missing pagination and the missing cap are closed together.
findings.patchBefore:
# application.yml — no pagination limits configured
spring:
  jpa:
    open-in-view: false
# (no spring.data.web.pageable.* keys present anywhere)
findings.patchAfter:
# application.yml
spring:
  data:
    web:
      pageable:
        default-page-size: 20
        max-page-size: 100   # resolver clamps any client-supplied ?size= to <=100
  jpa:
    open-in-view: false

// AuditLogController.java (hand-rolled size) — clamp explicitly
int safeSize = Math.min(Math.max(size, 1), 100);
return service.list(actionType, sourceModule, severity, page, safeSize);
references: OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023) API4:2023 Unrestricted Resource Consumption

findings.title: Cyber & SCM expose explicit '/all' register dumps (assets, controls, vendors) that bypass the module's own pagination
findings.category: Unbounded result set / intentional full-dump endpoint without cap
findings.cvss: Low: these endpoints are deliberately unpaged for UI dropdowns, but they carry no server-side row cap, so they grow unbounded with the asset/control/vendor inventory. Lower severity because they are typically backing select boxes (smaller cardinality and used less often than the main register), but they still allow a full-table fetch on demand.
findings.description: Several modules pair a properly-paginated register endpoint with an explicit '/all' (or root) variant that returns the entire org-scoped set, for populating UI dropdowns. CyberController exposes GET /api/v1/cyber/controls (Page<CyberControl>) alongside GET /api/v1/cyber/controls/all (List<CyberControl>), and GET /api/v1/cyber/assets (Page) alongside GET /api/v1/cyber/assets/all (List), plus GET /api/v1/cyber/frameworks (List). Each '/all' calls cyberService.getAllControls/getAllAssets/getFrameworks which delegate to controlRepo/assetRepo/frameworkRepo.findAllByOrganisationId(orgId) — repository finders that return List with no Pageable. ScmController.allVendors() is documented '/vendors/all — List all vendors (no pagination — for dropdowns)'. The asset inventory in particular (regulator-grade asset register) can grow very large, so a dropdown that fetches every asset is unbounded.
findings.rootCause: Intentional convenience endpoints for select-box population that were never given an upper bound. The repository exposes both findByOrganisationId(orgId, Pageable) and an unbounded findAllByOrganisationId(orgId); the '/all' endpoints deliberately call the unbounded one.
findings.impact: On large tenants a dropdown population request pulls the entire asset/control/vendor inventory into memory and over the wire. For the cyber asset register (which the platform markets as regulator-grade and can hold thousands of assets) this is a meaningful per-request cost and another path to the PERF-PG-001 heap-pressure problem, even though the main register endpoint is paginated.
findings.reproduction: 1. Seed many cyber assets for organisation_id = 1. 2. Call GET /api/v1/cyber/assets/all. 3. Observe the full asset set is returned with no page envelope and no size cap, regardless of how many rows exist (contrast GET /api/v1/cyber/assets which caps at 20).
findings.resolution: Cap the '/all' endpoints server-side. Prefer returning a lightweight projection (id + label only) for dropdowns and hard-limit the row count (e.g. PageRequest.of(0, 500)); if a register legitimately exceeds the cap, the UI should switch to a server-side type-ahead search endpoint instead of a full dump. At minimum add an explicit limit so the query can never fetch the entire table.
references: OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023) API4:2023 Unrestricted Resource Consumption
